cultures.name: Ancient Greek (Hesiodic)
cultures.overview: The days of the month as Hesiod's poem Works and Days (around 700 BCE) describes them: one farmer-poet's advice, not a calendar every Greek city kept.

systems.name: Works and Days: the days of the month
systems.description: Hesiod's list of good and bad days of the lunar month for farm work, crafts and household rites.
systems.month_rule: Hesiod counts a lunar month of about 30 days, partly in three ten-day parts ("the middle sixth" is the sixth day of the middle part). When his month began is not stated.
systems.uncertainty: One poet's prescriptions, not universal Greek practice. Not placed on modern dates.

systems.name: Calendar of lucky and unlucky days
systems.description: Papyri that rate days of the civil calendar as good, bad or mixed, often by reference to events in the myths of the gods.
systems.uncertainty: Days of the 365-day civil calendar. Placing one on a modern date needs a specific historical calendar and epoch; the museum description used here does not list the days.

systems.name: Hawaiian seasonal months
systems.description: Named lunar months of the Hawaiian year, each bounded by new Moons and linked to seasonal signs at sea and on land.
systems.uncertainty: These describe Hawaiʻi's seasons; they don't carry over to East Africa. The source is a university compilation.
